tiers.description: Deterministic CPU reference execution: simforge.compile/v1, simforge.simulate/v1, simforge.episode-batch/v1 in the runner binary. No GPU, driver or Python requirement.

blockers: fresh-install gate: package-runtime.sh + install-runtime.sh on a clean root, then `runtime show` with components installed:true
end-to-end gate: simforge.compile/v1 -> simforge.simulate/v1 -> in-process evaluate on a real published map/scenario through the installed binary, artifact hashes verified by `job artifacts`
runner crash/reconnect/cancel gates on the installed binary (detach, SIGKILL owner, worker reconcile, resume, cancel at safe boundary)
observed: isolated lifecycle tests (8) passed against a counting engine in a /tmp copy on 2026-09-05; not the installed binary
core/session unit tests reported by their owners; narrower than the end-to-end gate

tiers.description: Python providers installed into <root>/venv from the bundled wheels by install-runtime.sh; required by every provider workload.

blockers: install-runtime.sh must build <root>/venv from the bundled wheels on a clean host and import every provider module
one provider job (simforge.articulated-mujoco/v1 mujoco-cpu) must complete through the installed runner with verified artifacts
observed: Main ran the simforge_oss_physics job CLI directly (seeds 3,4; 120 decisions; 4 checkpoints); not through the installed runner

tiers.description: simforge.articulated-mujoco/v1 with backend mujoco-cpu (float64, same-build replay).

blockers: adapters/physics qualification gates (simforge-oss-physics qualify) must pass on the packaged wheel

tiers.description: simforge.articulated-mujoco/v1 with backend mujoco-warp: CUDA GPU with a driver supporting warp-lang; CPU/Warp parity is measured, not presumed.

blockers: mujoco-warp gates and measured CPU/Warp divergence on a real device

tiers.description: simforge.gpu-batch-rollout/v1 (roadway-dynamic-gpu-v1): Warp/CUDA device batches with binary64 arithmetic; cross-backend conformance is measured by qualification.

blockers: simforge-oss-gpu-conformance and qualify on a real device

tiers.description: simforge.render-bundle/v1: resident Bevy renderer (native-render-service + libsimforge_render.so, Bevy 0.19.1 / wgpu 29) on a Vulkan-capable GPU; gpu-interop device path requires CUDA and a matching physical device, otherwise the declared host-copy path is used.

blockers: captured frames must be non-blank and change with the scene (visual inspection), not merely byte-parity or a successful build
complete resource closure: share/sky plates present and digest-verified, scene assets resolvable from the runtime root
qualification.evidence: set by Main after real scene renders are inspected
observed: CUDA transport/lease mechanics passed but the captured image was black; transport mechanics are not visual qualification

tiers.description: NuRec reconstructed-world rendering via simforge-oss-splat: the wheel installs into <root>/venv, but CUDA PyTorch, a compiled 3DGRUT checkout (THREEDGRUT_ROOT), Kaolin, SHA-256 pinned NuRec .usdz packages, imported scene bundles, GLB catalog roots and a hood overlay profile are external prerequisites reported by `capabilities`, never assumed.

requires.assets: pinned .usdz packages, scenes root, catalog roots, hood dir

blockers: provider capabilities available:true on the target host and inspected non-blank renders
